name: North gate
period: late 3rd century AD (c. 270–280): the stone wall as newly built, all gates open
conventions: u along the town wall, v out to the field (so the "n" drawing is the field front); metres; origin the anchor corner

rooms.name: Gate passage
rooms.note: "covered passage (originally)" (1890, Pl. XXXI); roadway of flints 12 in thick, gravelled (1890)

rooms.name: Approach between the flanks
rooms.note: narrowing from 36 ft to 22 ft and then 10 ft before the gate (1890)

walls.note: western flank: the curtain turned inward, "an inward sweep of the curtain wall" (Fox & St John Hope 1890); it meets the gate at an angle, perhaps a change of plan (1890)

openings.note: outer arch, about 11 ft wide and 2½ ft deep; the double doors hung immediately behind it on pivots in a timber sill (1890). outer arch carried up as a crenellated parapet on the platform's field side (the parapet: comparison)
inner arch, about 11 ft wide and 2½ ft deep (1890)

platforms.note: "the large platform over the gate itself would enable the defenders to pass from one side to the other" (Fox & St John Hope 1890); at the walk's level, on timber over the passage (the report leaves timber or vault open)
